newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama's new bank law to be ready in June-official.
newsitem.headline: Panama's new bank law to be ready in June-official.

text.p: A draft of Panama's new banking law to prevent money laundering should be ready next month and take effect later this year, a top government official said Tuesday.

The new law should be made public next month for consultation, then sent to Congress for passage in September or October, said Miguel Lee, deputy general manager of Banco Nacional de Panama, the country's central bank.
The new law will increase capital requirements and strengthen auditing procedures, he said.

"We want fewer but stronger banks," he said. "We have more than 100 banks. We don't want to have banks just for the sake of having banks. Obviously some banks will have to merge with stronger banks or put in more capital," he said.
The changes call for the creation of an independent banking commission with broader powers to supervise local banks and the authority to shut down troubled institutions, he said.
Current laws prevent the banking commission from intervening in troubled banks.

Lee said the changes also call for increasing capital requirements for banks, raising the amount to establish a bank in Panama from $3 million to perhaps as high as $20 million, and requiring banks to make quarterly audits.
Currently, banks are not required by law to disclose their assets, he said.
